title: A dipolar Bose-Bose mixture of Dysprosium isotopes with controllable interspecies interactions
authors: M. Duerbeck, L. Reihs, J. P. Marulanda-Serna, B. Choudhari, J. Seifert, N. Werum, G. Meijer, G. Valtolina
abstract: We report on the realization of a quantum-degenerate Bose-Bose mixture of 162Dy and 164Dy. Owing to the near-identical mass and polarizability of the two isotopes, the mixture thermalizes efficiently, with evaporation trajectories closely following those of the single-isotope case. Using a broad interspecies Feshbach resonance, we explore a miscible-immiscible transition between the two Bose-Einstein condensates. The tunability of the interspecies interaction, combined with the large magnetic dipole moment of Dy, makes this platform well suited for exploring dipolar effects in ultracold mixtures, including multi-component supersolidity.
summary: The paper reports on creating and characterizing a quantum-degenerate Bose-Bose mixture of Dysprosium isotopes, which serves as a highly controllable platform for studying dipolar physics. By tuning interspecies interactions via Feshbach resonances, the researchers observed evidence of a transition between miscible and immiscible phases in the condensate cloud. This work advances the understanding of complex many-body dynamics in dipolar quantum gases.
main_problem: The study investigates dipolar effects and the miscibility transition within a quantum-degenerate Bose-Bose mixture of Dysprosium isotopes.
main_result: The authors demonstrated efficient thermalization in the mixture and provided evidence for an interaction-driven spatial reorganization, consistent with tuning across a miscible-immiscible crossover.
method: Experiments involved evaporative cooling followed by atom-loss spectroscopy as a function of magnetic field to probe interspecies interactions and center-of-mass separation measurements.
model_or_system: The platform is a quantum-degenerate Bose-Bose mixture of $^{162}	ext{Dy}$ and $^{164}	ext{Dy}$, which possesses large magnetic dipole moments, making it ideal for studying dipolar interactions in ultracold gases.
key_observables: Center-of-mass separation ($\Delta y$), atom loss spectra, and the efficiency of evaporative cooling ($\gamma$).
important_parameters: The interspecies scattering length ($a_{12}$), controlled via broad Feshbach resonances; magnetic field strength (e.g., near 9.7 G).
main_assumptions: Efficient thermalization is assumed, although isotope-specific three-body losses were noted as a potential limitation.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate population control via detuning ($\delta EOM$), compare mixture vs. single-species atom-loss spectra to find resonances, and plot relative vertical displacement ($\Delta y$) versus magnetic field to show phase separation behavior.
paper_structure: The work progresses from establishing the stable cooling and thermalization of the dual-isotope mixture, to mapping out interspecies Feshbach resonances using loss spectroscopy, culminating in measurements that probe spatial reorganization indicative of a miscibility crossover.
why_interesting: This research directly addresses advanced many-body physics in ultracold atomic systems by incorporating long-range dipolar interactions and exploring complex phase transitions like supersolidity and immiscibility.

(a) & (c) show the single- isotope atom-loss spectra over 2.6-7 G and 8.5-12.1 G for 162Dy (green) and 164Dy (orange), recorded at 1 µK with a 1 s hold time. (b) shows the atom-loss spectra of the 162Dy-164Dy mixture over the same field range, recorded at 300 nK with a 500 ms hold time. Shaded regions highlight interspecies resonances. A broad resonance, extending from approximately 10.1 to 11.95 G, is centered at B0 = 10.8(3) G, offering the opportunity to easily control the interspecies scattering length a12 in the Bose-Bose mixture.
